regression.before: A vector scanner returning two rows for batchSize(1) caused a two-row projected yield. Both abort and early-close cases failed the new public-API matrix before the runtime change.
regression.mechanism: Projection and materialization operated on the entire scanner batch before enforcing an output boundary.

fix: Generic positioned vector batching slices oversized inputs before projected execution and deferred gather consumers, preserving physical row offsets.
Scoped vector slicing admits records, typed views, nested struct directories and copied legacy reference arrays before construction; payload and list/map/dictionary children remain borrowed.
Owned slices retain both input backing and slice metadata; borrowed slices detach selected output before scanner advancement.
Projection offset/limit slices also use scoped admission. Complete batches reuse input identity without additional slice allocation.
evidence: Ten public stream cases cover row projection, row ordering, row windows, vector projection and vector windows, each with abort or early closure; paused expanded strings remain charged.
A 1000-row borrowed vector input expands each row to 10000 characters while yielding one row at a time under a 128 KiB shared pool; completion releases all charges.

Helper cases cover short final batches, physical offsets, independent retained owners, exact capacity/cap-minus-one, sibling preservation, abort before/during iteration, empty inputs and whole-batch reuse.
Scoped slice exact-cap tests cover numeric, nullable boolean, legacy text/binary arrays, nested lists/structs, packed text and signed 96-bit timestamps.

Real Parquet HTTP 206/200 fixtures deliberately return larger scanner batches for both borrowed and owned routes; filtered offset/limit output matches an independent row oracle and stays within batchSize(3). Cache eviction releases remaining charges.

validation.workerRetry: Concurrent run had entrypoint import (15s) and NDJSON (5s) timeouts; complete isolated rerun passed with original timeouts unchanged.

boundaries: Third-party scanners remain responsible for allocations made before yielding; downstream slicing cannot retroactively bound those allocations.
Slices retain source backing while exposed; this avoids copying payload but does not shrink the source allocation.
HTTP fixture checks are local network transport tests, not live R2 or whole-isolate heap measurements.
Whole-runtime headroom, remaining audit findings and final complete release-gate refresh remain open.
